::: {.callout-note}
**Coming soon.** A worked example of using Claude Code on the perpetual
small jobs of teaching: refreshing slides, writing problem sets,
maintaining a syllabus, generating solutions and grading rubrics.
:::

## Outline

1. **Beamer slides.** "Look at last year's slide deck for Lecture 4. Update
   the dates, the example dataset URL, and the news clipping on slide 17.
   Don't change the content otherwise." Read the diff before compiling.
2. **Problem sets.** "Write a problem set on instrumental variables that
   builds on the material in `lecture05.tex`. Five problems, increasing
   difficulty. Provide a separate solution file."
3. **Solutions and rubrics.** Have Claude work each problem and produce
   step-by-step solutions plus a point-allocation rubric. **Verify each
   solution yourself** before posting — the model can confidently produce
   wrong answers.
4. **Syllabus maintenance.** "Update the reading list to include three
   recent (2024–2026) papers on the topics in weeks 7–9. List the citations
   and one-sentence relevance for each. Don't add anything to the syllabus
   yet."
5. **Reusing previous semesters.** Point Claude at last year's full course
   directory and your current `_quarto.yml` (or whatever you use). Have
   it propose a refresh.

## Notes (will be expanded)

- For LaTeX/Beamer, the [LaTeX paper editing](latex-paper.qmd) example
  applies almost verbatim.
- For Quarto-based teaching sites (like your `metrics-phd-course`),
  Claude is well-suited to keeping `_quarto.yml`, sidebar, and weekly
  pages in sync.
- Solutions you generate **must be checked**. A wrong solution posted to
  students costs more time than you saved generating it.

> Tell me which step you'd most like worked through.
